card.grading: The gate is the optimal cost, which must equal the known best on every hidden instance that the base solves. The score is the total time (median over repeated runs) with timeouts counted against a fixed cap, against the reference speedup S, as 2^u - 1.
card.reference: We use a later release of the same engine, or our own tuned build, measured on the hidden families. The speedup is measured on the instance set and the size is not found yet.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agent performance on this work; capped at 3 by rule.

Build.why: Makefile C++ engine plus harness is likely under 5 days; no smoke build was run, so the estimate is unverified.

Fit.why: CPU C++ engine within 8 cores and 16 GB; a 1.5 GB sample fits, but the full data (58.9 GB) must not ship.

Hor.why: Propagation layout, clause DB, preprocessing and parallelism need sustained profiling over 8h.

Lic.why: Zenodo CC-BY-4.0 is confirmed, but the Open-WBO licence wording is unverified and instance-level licences are not found.

Multi.why: Several levers and families, but total time is dominated by a few long instances, so credit is less dense than the seed claims.

Nov.why: Nearest neighbour 0.195 (S-op-014) is above 0.15 so it is not a 5; MaxSAT is not on the CROWDED list.

Real.why: Real MSE collection and real sat-group repo; the exact later-release reference is not yet confirmed.

Ref.why: A later release or tuned build could reach a meaningful S, but it is unmeasured and the public later release is unverified.

Seal.why: Hidden renamed instances plus model-checked costs close caching; a history-less snapshot is needed if the later release is public.

Surf.why: Hidden instance families across years could be thousands with an executable model-check oracle; the count is not verified.

spike_plan.kill_if: Base solves almost none of the sample; no later or tuned reference reaches S above 1.1; repeat CV above 20% so timing cannot be graded; or costs cannot be checked against a known best.
spike_plan.pass_if: Build green; base solves a meaningful share of sample instances; costs match best-known; repeat CV under 10%; a reference or tuned build gives S of at least 1.3 with matching costs.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone sat-group/open-wbo at a pinned commit and build it with make; record the build result and time.
Obtain the 2017 weighted sample from Zenodo 2017.zip, count instances, and record best-known costs from the MSE 2017 results.
Run the base binary on about 10 sample instances with a fixed timeout, 5 repeats each; record per-instance median wall time and whether each cost matches the best-known value.
Check run-to-run variance (coefficient of variation) of total time across repeats under gVisor-like conditions if available, or in the container.
Obtain a later release (verify whether an Open-WBO-Inc fork is public) or a quick tuned build (-O3, LTO, clause-DB reduction flag) and measure the speedup S on the same sample.
Decide: if S is above 1.3 with matching costs and CV under 10%, pass; otherwise record the headroom and the cause.

v1.summary: The Zenodo MSE collection (CC-BY-4.0) and the Open-WBO and RC2/PySAT engines are real and public, so the seed passes the real-source gate, but the instance count, Open-WBO licence wording and later-release reference are not yet verified. No kill gate fails on current evidence, so the idea passes to a spike focused on reference S, timing noise and cost agreement, with E0 evidence and a Band capped at 3.

v2.note: There is no reference. No later Open-WBO release or fork was verified, no speedup S was measured, and the 'own tuned build' is hypothetical. Several facts are unconfirmed: the engine licence (Open-WBO wording not found), the instance-level licences, and the instance count. Multi-minute solver runs under gVisor make wall-clock timing noisy (K4 risk). The base must also be chosen so it solves a meaningful share of instances while leaving headroom. Revisit only with a measured S of at least 1.3 and a confirmed permissive engine.
